Quiet Table, second pass

One board for the whole game. The working interface stays plain. The arcane look marks what you hold and the big moments. This pass takes the arcane look further than the first Quiet Table did, and it gives every painting a fixed place.

The first Quiet Table had one rule: if a thing tells you something, it is plain; if you hold it, it is engraved. This pass keeps that rule and adds three things.

  • A third material for moments and faces. The lapis ribbon of the wonder plate becomes a part of the kit. It appears at three weights: a hairline under a sheet head, a band behind a face, and the full sash behind a painting.
  • One window for every painting. An ink line, a gap of paper, then a gilt line. The same window holds the fallback when there is no painting, so no screen has two layouts.
  • Two more card forms. A great person is a tall card with an arched window for a face. A government is a banner. Resources, technologies, buildings and units stay plain.

Your paintings share three colours with the game: the lapis of the sky, the cream of the stone and the orange of the light. The interface already has lapis, parchment and cinnabar. So a painting sits well on a parchment sheet and on the lapis ribbon. It sits badly on the dark cloth. For that reason the dark cloth stays on the Council, In play and the star chart, and goes no further.

Where the amount of arcane is a real choice, the frame is drawn twice: quiet and richer. Comment by id, for example "frame-2-richer".

The "today" pictures are from the current build (branch decks, 19 November), a bot game at turn 101, at 1440 by 900. The age plate and the Opus close are pictures from 18 November. The mock-ups are drawn in HTML at 1000 px wide. The map behind them is a screenshot. The typefaces load from Google Fonts and are the game's own six faces; if your browser blocks them, a close system stack takes their place. Card texts, costs and figures are samples.

Not drawn on this board: belief vignettes (they wait for the belief marks), a capital taken and a seat eliminated (they can reuse the ribbon plate with one generic painting each), and discovery claims.

The rules of the style

  1. Paper is the working interface. Panels, sheets, lists, tables, tooltips and buttons are flat parchment with ink text. Every counted figure is tabular mono.
  2. Engraving marks what you hold. An Order, a Doctrine, a government, a wonder, a belief, a great person and a legacy have an engraved card, piece or seal. Their names are in the small-caps card face.
  3. A technology, a resource, a building and a unit are never engraved. They are rows with a flat mark.
  4. Lapis and gilt mark a moment or a face. The ribbon has three weights: a hairline under a sheet head, a band behind a portrait, the full sash behind a plate. A full lapis page is for an age and for a win.
  5. Gilt is a hairline, never a fill, outside a card. It frames a painting, edges a panel that holds a held thing, and outlines a button on lapis or cloth.
  6. A painting appears only in the window (ink line, gap, gilt line), and only for a wonder, a leader, a great person, a government, an age, the title and the ending. Never on a control, a table or a tooltip.
  7. Every window has a fallback of the same size: a seal, an emblem or a charge on an engraved ground.
  8. The dark cloth is the card table: the Council, In play and the star chart. It goes no further, unless you choose the richer offer (frame 6).
  9. The sun, the moon and the star have meanings: yours or ready, another court or waiting, a capital or a list mark.
  10. These never change: the ink top bar, the cinnabar End turn, the next step at the bottom right, the × to close, plain words, and the town banners on the map.

What I recommend, and a build order

Levels. Take quiet for the HUD (frame 1), with one part of the richer level: the painting in the wonder toast. The HUD is on the map all game and the map must stay the brightest thing. Take richer for the city screen and for diplomacy (frames 2 and 5): you step away from the board there, and the forms are ones the game already has. Take quiet for the offers (frame 6): a paper sheet over the map keeps the board in view while you choose. Take form B for the age plate (frame 8).

StageWhatSizeNeeds

2 · Wonders in listsThe painting in the city build list, on the item in work, and in the star chart's panel. The star chart's panel itself.Small to mediumStage 1

Questions for you
